note: Built retrospectively on 2026-08-03 from the already-extracted fact store (facts/financials.json) and cache/markdown, to prove the v2 spine end-to-end. In a normal run this file is written at wave 1.5, BEFORE extraction, so it can steer extraction depth. Written after the fact here, it inherits whatever extraction already captured — which is exactly why several kpi_tree entries below are computable:false with the missing input named. Provenance for the sector method: prompts/sector_playbooks/ferrous_non_ferrous_metals.md.

identity.summary: NALCO mines bauxite, refines it into alumina, and smelts a minority of that alumina into primary aluminium, selling both alumina (largely exported, priced off a percentage of LME) and aluminium metal (priced off LME plus premia). It earns a conversion spread on a globally priced commodity it cannot price, so its economics are cost position plus the LME.
identity.listing: NSE/BSE; ticker NATIONALUM.NS (NOT 'NALCO.NS' — tools/market_data.py returns nothing for the wrong symbol and fails silently)
identity.basis_note: Standalone is primary. The segment note, production and capacity tables are all standalone; consolidated adds only small JV/associate effects. Triage T3 recorded that both reportable segments sit in one aluminium value chain.
identity.promoter_type: PSU — Government of India majority shareholder

value_chain.detail: Panchpatmali captive mine, ~7.5 MTPA current capacity; FY2022 production 7,511,075 t. Pottangi is the next lease, guided to operationalise April 2026.
Damanjodi refinery, ~2.1 MTPA current capacity; FY2022 alumina production 2,122,000 t. A 5th stream adds ~1.0 MTPA, guided March 2026 commissioning / April 2026 production.
1,200 MW captive thermal plant at Angul plus 198.4 MW wind. Coal is the exposure: Utkal coal blocks guided to ~4 mt in FY2026. Power and fuel was INR 3,388.48 cr in FY2022.
Angul smelter, ~0.46 MTPA; FY2022 production 460,000 t — i.e. the smelter consumes under half the refinery's alumina output.

Predominantly EXPORT, on tenders priced as a percentage of LME aluminium. FY2022 export 1,154,691 t vs domestic 77,995 t — a ~94% export share, which is the single most important structural fact about this company.
Domestic and export sales of ingots/wire rod/rolled products, priced off LME plus regional premium, less discounts.

margin_pool.narrative: The rent sits at ALUMINA REFINING, not at smelting. NALCO owns a captive bauxite mine feeding a refinery whose cash cost sits in the low quartiles of the global cost curve, and it sells the surplus alumina — roughly three-quarters of refinery output — into an export market priced off LME. Smelting, by contrast, converts that same alumina plus 1,200 MW of coal-fired power into metal at a spread that a domestic private peer with cheaper power can beat. So the economic engine is: a low-cost, long-position alumina business subsidising a structurally average smelter. FY2025 makes it visible — Chemical segment result INR 3,245.0 cr on revenue INR 7,607.44 cr (42.7% margin) against Aluminium's INR 4,045.51 cr on INR 11,113.16 cr (36.4%), and the Chemical margin swings far harder with alumina price.
margin_pool.bottleneck_reason: Captive bauxite at a grade and strip ratio that a non-integrated refiner cannot replicate, plus a lease it already holds. The durability question is the lease pipeline (Pottangi) and coal, not the refinery.

long: alumina price (surplus alumina sold into export tenders as a % of LME)
exposed_to: coal availability from Utkal blocks and e-auction premia
mining lease and forest clearance timelines
net_position.single_most_important_tilt: NET LONG ALUMINA. The refinery is ~2.1 MTPA against a 0.46 MTPA smelter, so roughly three-quarters of alumina output is sold rather than converted, and ~94% of that is exported. NALCO is therefore better described as a low-cost alumina exporter with a smelter attached than as an aluminium producer — and the Emkay benchmark's whole thesis was exactly this phrase.

Unit profitability of the metal leg; the Emkay benchmark's Exhibit 20 is exactly this series for alumina vs aluminium over a decade.

kpi_tree.missing_input: a capacity fact in the SAME unit as production. `capacity_alumina` (F-AR22-068) is recorded as value 2275 with unit 'lakh TPA', which is wrong — 2275 is thousand-TPA (2.275 MTPA), consistent with `alumina_refinery_capacity_current` = 2.1 MTPA (F-PQ1-066). Dividing 2,122,000 tonnes by 2275 yields 93,275%, so this must not be computed until the capacity fact's unit is corrected by re-extraction.

Its inputs (`ebit`, `capital_employed`) are not separate fact records, so restating it as a kpi_tree quotient duplicates work and resolves to nothing. kpi_tree.why_it_matters: This sector's equity risk is refinancing at the trough. NALCO is net cash, which is itself a thesis point — but it must be stated at mid-cycle EBITDA, not spot.

unit_economics.known_limitation: Production facts were extracted for FY2022 only (F-AR22-050/051/052, standalone). FY2024 carries the same quantities under different metric names (`alumina_hydrate_production_mt`, `aluminium_production_mt`, basis 'na') and FY2025/FY2026 under a third naming convention in '000T on a consolidated basis. So per-tonne series resolve for FY2022 and then break. Fixing this is a naming-normalisation task for extraction, and it is the reason the per-unit KPIs below emit for one year rather than five.

peer_set.comparability_delta: Integrated but Novelis-dominated — majority of EBITDA is downstream rolled products in the US/EU, so the aluminium-cycle beta is far lower. Not a clean read-across.
Largest Indian primary smelter but alumina-SHORT (buys third-party alumina), so it is on the opposite side of NALCO's core exposure. The most informative peer precisely for that reason.
Same promoter-group structure and PSU-adjacent history, different metal. Useful only for capital-allocation and dividend-policy comparison.
The closest global analogue for a bauxite-alumina-aluminium integrated producer with surplus alumina; USD reporting and different power mix.
Integrated with hydro power — a structurally lower-carbon, lower-cost energy position, so it sets the benchmark NALCO's coal-fired power is measured against.
Alumina-long diversified miner; its alumina segment disclosure is a good source for cost-curve and realisation benchmarking.
Sets the marginal cost and the export behaviour that drives the alumina balance; state-linked, so its capacity decisions are not purely economic.

business_model_summary: NALCO mines bauxite, refines ~2.1 MTPA of alumina, and smelts only ~0.46 MTPA into metal — so roughly three-quarters of alumina output is sold, ~94% of it exported on percentage-of-LME tenders.
Single most important structural tilt: NET LONG ALUMINA. It is a low-cost alumina exporter with a smelter attached, not an aluminium producer.
The rent sits at refining, on captive Panchpatmali bauxite; the smelter's spread is average and coal-exposed.
Three KPIs that matter most: alumina EBIT per tonne; alumina realisation as a percentage of LME; power and fuel per tonne of aluminium.
Three swing drivers: alumina percentage-of-LME realisation; LME aluminium; captive coal availability (Utkal).
The 5th stream (+1.0 MTPA, guided April 2026) amplifies the alumina tilt rather than diversifying it.
Balance sheet is net cash — unusual for the sector, and a real thesis point, but it must be stated against mid-cycle EBITDA.
Biggest data gap: no cash cost of production per tonne was extracted, so the cost-curve claim cannot yet be evidenced.
